p1_findings.title: Reviewed preflight identities are not rechecked at the one-shot consumption boundary
evidence: Runner lines 58-63 correctly require both reviewer-supplied preflight SHA roots.
Runner lines 193-202 correctly verify the nested seals and compare both reviewed identities.
Runner then starts a separate semantic-check Python process at lines 203-223.
The next operation is mkdir(attempt) at line 225; there is no second receipt/outer digest comparison after the semantic process and immediately before mkdir.
This is narrower than M672 P1, but does not implement M672's explicit minimum repair requiring a second comparison at the attempt boundary.
p1_findings.impact: A concurrent replacement after the first SHA comparison can preserve the small semantic subset checked by the Python process while changing the reviewed receipt or outer-seal identity before one-shot consumption. The externally reviewed identity therefore is not guaranteed to be the identity present at mkdir(attempt).
minimum_repair: Keep the existing post-seal two-SHA comparison.
Repeat the same receipt and outer-seal-file digest comparison after the semantic Python checker returns and immediately before mkdir(attempt).
On either mismatch, exit 41 while attempt and output remain absent.
Preserve both expected values in the initial double-sealed attempt receipt.

decision.reason: M674 permits GO only with P0=0 and P1=0; this review has P1=1.
